title: Storefront returns 502
summary: Users see 502 Bad Gateway after an application change. Find why the proxy cannot reach the application and restore checkout without taking the proxy down.
learningObjectives: Trace a 502 response from the reverse proxy to its upstream.
Compare the configured upstream with the sockets that services actually listen on.
Validate proxy configuration before applying it, and prefer a reload to a restart.

provenance.notes: Draft written to prove the environment contract. A common upstream misconfiguration, not adapted from a specific incident report.

alert.title: Checkout error rate above 90%
alert.summary: Synthetic checkout checks have returned 502 Bad Gateway from the storefront since the latest application deploy.

plantedFault.summary: nginx proxy_pass targets 127.0.0.1:8081, but the application now listens on 127.0.0.1:8080.

referenceFix.description: Point proxy_pass at port 8080, validate the configuration, and reload.

traps.description: Restarting nginx after an edit that breaks its configuration stops the proxy, so 502 responses become refused connections.

safeAlternative.description: A reload with the same broken configuration fails and keeps the running workers, so the proxy stays up.

hints.text: The proxy is answering, so its error log should say which upstream address it is trying to reach.
Compare the upstream in the proxy configuration with the sockets that are listening, for example with ss -ltnp.

debrief.rootCause: The application moved to port 8080, but nginx still proxies to 127.0.0.1:8081 where nothing listens, so every proxied request fails with 502 Bad Gateway.
causalChain: An application change moved the service from port 8081 to port 8080.
The nginx upstream still targets port 8081.
Connections to port 8081 are refused, and nginx answers every proxied request with 502 Bad Gateway.

keyEvidence.description: The nginx error log shows refused connections to upstream 127.0.0.1:8081.
The socket list shows the application listening on port 8080, not 8081.
The nginx configuration sets proxy_pass to port 8081.

recommendedRecovery: Read the nginx error log to identify the failing upstream address.
Confirm which port the application listens on with ss -ltnp.
Change proxy_pass to port 8080 and run nginx -t.
Apply the change with nginx -s reload and watch the error rate fall.
